artists.biography: Cardiacs are an English band formed in 1977 and led by Tim Smith. Noted for their complex, varied and intense compositional style and for their eccentric, theatrical stage shows, they have been hailed as an influence by many newer groups and artists.  Their music combines the excitement and energy of punk with the intricacies and technical cleverness of early British progressive rock, a combination sometimes referred to as pronk, although frontman Tim Smith has disavowed this classification.  Cardiacs have released eight studio albums plus a number of live albums, compilation albums and singles between 1980 and 2007, and are best known for the 1988 minor hit single "Is This the Life?" They are also noted for attracting strongly diverse responses: they have remained one of Britain's leading cult rock bands during their four-decade-spanning career, but have also attracted virulent critical attack (including a lengthy editorial ban from the British music magazine New Musical Express).  The band has been on indefinite (and possibly permanent) hiatus following the 2008 hospitalisation of Tim Smith after a heart attack and series of strokes.

perplexity.description:
A Little Man and a House and the Whole World Window is the debut studio album by English progressive rock band Cardiacs, released in 1988. Recorded between 1985 and 1987, the album showcases the band's distinctive approach to avant-garde and RIO (Rock in Opposition) influenced progressive rock. The eleven-track collection demonstrates the compositional complexity and theatrical intensity that would define Cardiacs' reputation, featuring extended instrumental passages and intricate arrangements across tracks like the title track and "In A City Lining."

As Cardiacs' first official studio release, the album established the band's signature sound following their earlier EPs and cassette releases. The record captures Tim Smith's vision for the group's elaborate, multi-layered compositions, blending progressive rock structures with unconventional song arrangements. The album's reception within progressive rock circles was significant, contributing to Cardiacs' status as a cult act whose influence would eventually extend to diverse artists including Blur, Faith No More, and Radiohead.

The album remains a cornerstone of the band's discography, representing their early artistic statement before subsequent releases like On Land and in the Sea (1989) and Songs for Ships and Irons (1991). Its combination of technical proficiency and experimental sensibility established Cardiacs as one of the UK's most distinctive progressive rock acts, appealing primarily to dedicated listeners of avant-garde and complex rock music rather than achieving mainstream commercial success.
